# UI-UX Principles: knowledge-base index

90 principles and 125 source examples extracted from *The UI/UX Playbook: Tips & Tricks for Exceptional Design* (uxpeak, 144-page PDF). IDs are stable; cite them in reviews together with the PDF page.

How to use:
1. Find candidate principles in [task-router.md](task-router.md) (by UI element/task) or in the table below.
2. Open only the chapter files you need; each entry has the PDF statement, mistake, correction, observable checks, exceptions and examples.
3. Anything not from the PDF lives in [supplemental.md](supplemental.md) and must be labelled as supplemental.
4. Page-by-page provenance: coverage-map.md (optional `ui-ux-playbook-visuals` pack). Ambiguities and source errors: [source-notes.md](source-notes.md). All images: examples-gallery.md (optional `ui-ux-playbook-visuals` pack).

Page numbers: PDF page (printed page = PDF page - 1).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FND-01](principles/01-foundations.md#fnd-01) | Get both UI and UX right | 3, 4, 5 | Every interface, especially first-impression surfaces such as landing pages and hero sections that must also let users act. | 3 |
| [FND-02](principles/01-foundations.md#fnd-02) | Treat these guidelines as a foundation, then test with users | 143 | Whenever conclusions from this playbook are used to justify a design decision. | 0 |

## Interaction cost - [16-interaction-cost.md](principles/16-interaction-cost.md)

| ID | Principle | PDF pages | Applies when | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [IC-01](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-01) | Reduce interaction cost (cognitive, physical, time) | 98, 99 | Every flow; use it as the lens when evaluating tasks. | 1 |
| [IC-02](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-02) | Keep related actions close and large (Fitts's law) | 99, 100, 108 | Controls tied to specific content; persistent controls (e.g. media playback). | 2 |
| [IC-03](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-03) | Minimise choice | 101 | Catalogues and pages with many options. | 1 |
| [IC-04](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-04) | Chunk information to respect working memory | 101, 102, 123, 124, 125 | Long descriptions, product pages, listing pages. | 4 |
| [IC-05](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-05) | Reduce distractions during tasks | 103, 128, 129 | Reading experiences, sign-up, checkout and other task flows. | 3 |
| [IC-06](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-06) | Promote recognition over recall | 104 | Navigation, resumable tasks, history, settings. | 1 |
| [IC-07](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-07) | Streamline tasks: remove or combine steps | 105, 109 | Checkout, onboarding, data entry. | 2 |
| [IC-08](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-08) | Reduce repetition | 106 | Bulk actions, repetitive data entry, power-user workflows. | 1 |
| [IC-09](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-09) | Expose options instead of hiding them in dropdowns | 107, 108 | Small option sets (colours, sizes, quantities) on product pages and forms. | 2 |
| [IC-10](principles/16-interaction-cost.md#ic-10) | Expose content directly instead of behind banners | 111, 112, 113 | Home/discover screens, onboarding, content apps. | 2 |
